proof.text: For a monotone map $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$, extend it to $\widehat\alpha:[n+2]\to[m+2]$ by $0\mapsto0$, $1\mapsto1$, $i+2\mapsto\alpha(i)+2$. These extensions respect identities and composition. Restricting $t$ along $\widehat\alpha$ preserves the fixed edge $s$ and the constant final face, so gives the stated simplicial set $T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)$. Omitting $0$ or $1$ leaves exactly a simplex with its first vertex $y$ or $x$ and its remaining face constant at $z$. These restrictions commute with the extensions of $\alpha$ fixing one first vertex. Thus $r_1$ and $r_0$ land in the left-pinched mapping spaces defined in [lem-coef-infinity-left-pinch-comparison] and are simplicial maps.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.8.16, proof, and Remark 4.6.8.17; Construction 4.6.8.9 and Notation 4.6.8.15.

proof.text: The map $r_1$ is a trivial Kan fibration. Indeed, a boundary-lifting problem of dimension $m$ consists of compatible simplices $t_i$ over the faces of $\Delta^m$ and a prescribed $m$-simplex of $L_{\mathcal E}(y,z)$. On $\Delta^{m+2}$ the $t_i$ prescribe the faces omitting $i+2$, and the prescribed simplex of $L(y,z)$ prescribes the face omitting $0$. Their intersections agree because the lifting square commutes. Together these are exactly all codimension-one faces except the face omitting $1$, hence the inner horn $\Lambda_1^{m+2}$. For $m=0$, the boundary is empty and the domain is instead the two edges $s$ on $01$ and the given arrow on $12$, again $\Lambda_1^2$. The quasicategory horn axiom fills this horn. The filler retains $s$ on $01$ and its final face is constantly $z$, since that face is already in the prescribed face omitting $0$. It is therefore a simplex of $T$ solving the problem. This proves surjectivity in degree zero and every boundary lifting required by [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration].

source.place: Proposition 4.6.8.16, proof, and Remark 4.6.8.17; Construction 4.6.8.9 and Notation 4.6.8.15.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-left-pinch-comparison], $L_{\mathcal E}(y,z)$ is Kan and $j^L:L_{\mathcal E}(y,z)\to U_{\mathcal E}(y,z)$ is a homotopy equivalence. To check that $T$ is Kan, map a horn in $T$ through $r_1$, fill it in $L(y,z)$, and lift this filled simplex back to $T$ using [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] for the degreewise injective horn inclusion. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] supplies a section and a simplicial homotopy inverse for $r_1$. Consequently the left roof leg $a=j^Lr_1$ is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes. All these assertions also hold with $\mathcal B,p(s),p(z)$ in place of $\mathcal E,s,z$.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.8.16, proof, and Remark 4.6.8.17; Construction 4.6.8.9 and Notation 4.6.8.15.

proof.text: Write $q_m:[2]\times[m]\to[m+2]$ for the map in the statement. It is monotone: its three rows have values $0$, $1$, and $i+2$, respectively, and each row is monotone with every value of a later row at least every value of an earlier row. Taking the induced map of standard simplicial sets gives $Q_m:\Delta^2\times\Delta^m\to\Delta^{m+2}$. For every monotone $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$, the equality $\widehat\alpha q_n=q_m(\mathrm{id}_{[2]}\times\alpha)$ holds on each pair $(k,i)$, separately for $k=0,1,2$. Hence $e_m(t)=tQ_m$ commutes with all simplicial operators. On the three vertex factors its values are constantly $x,y,z$, respectively, because the first two rows are constant vertices and the third row lies in the constant final face of $t$. The definition of $V(x,y,z)$ in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] therefore gives the simplicial map $e:T\to V(x,y,z)$.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.8.16, proof, and Remark 4.6.8.17; Construction 4.6.8.9 and Notation 4.6.8.15.

proof.text: Compute the three edge restrictions of $q_m$. On $01\times[m]$ it is $(0,i)\mapsto0$, $(1,i)\mapsto1$, so $tQ_m$ restricts to the constant $m$-simplex at the arrow $s$. On $12\times[m]$ the two rows are $1$ and $i+2$; after omitting vertex $0$ these are $0$ and $i+1$, exactly the left-pinch formula applied to $r_1(t)$. On $02\times[m]$ the two rows are $0$ and $i+2$; after omitting vertex $1$ they are again $0$ and $i+1$, the formula applied to $r_0(t)$. Thus, in the edge order $12,01$ specified by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], one has the strict equalities $\theta e=(j^Lr_1,c_s)$ and $\ell e=j^Lr_0$. This also shows that $e$ factors through the fiber of restriction to $01$ at $s$, so retains the specified triangle witness rather than only its edge classes.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.8.16, proof, and Remark 4.6.8.17; Construction 4.6.8.9 and Notation 4.6.8.15.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], $\theta$ is a homotopy equivalence and composition in arrow spaces is $[\ell][\theta]^{-1}$. Put $a=j^Lr_1$ and $b=j^Lr_0$. Step 5 gives $[\theta][e]=([a],[c_s])$ and $[b]=[\ell][e]$. Multiplying the first equality by $[\theta]^{-1}$ and substituting in the second gives exactly $[b]=[\ell][\theta]^{-1}([a],[c_s])$. No inverse on a mapping space is chosen to obtain the equality. The precomposition class $P_s$ is the restriction of the composition class to the vertex $s$, as specified by the cited node. Thus the equality reads $[b]=P_s[a]$. Since $a$ is invertible by Step 3, $[b][a]^{-1}=P_s$: the roof represents precomposition, with $e$ as its triangle witness. Homotopies may be precomposed with $e$ by composing their maps $V\times\Delta^1\to V$ with $e\times\mathrm{id}$; hence the class calculation is valid also before using that $T$ is Kan.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.8.16, proof, and Remark 4.6.8.17; Construction 4.6.8.9 and Notation 4.6.8.15.

proof.text: For a simplex $t$, postcomposition with the given simplicial map $p$ gives $(pt)Q_m=p(tQ_m)$. Similarly, restricting $pt$ to either face is $p$ applied to the restriction of $t$, and precomposing a restricted simplex with the left-pinch map commutes with postcomposition by $p$. These are the equalities $p e=e_{\mathcal B}p$, $p r_k=r_k p$ and $p j^L=j^L p$ degree by degree, and therefore equalities of simplicial maps. Moreover $p(c_s)=c_{p(s)}$, and restriction to each of $01,12,02$ commutes with $p$. Assemble these identities with Step 5: the roofs over $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal B$, their maps to the fixed-edge triangle spaces, and all three triangle boundary maps commute strictly under $p$. Applying Step 6 to both rows identifies these very roofs with precomposition by $s$ and $p(s)$, respectively. The maps between their triangle witnesses provide the commutation data of the precomposition square. This uses the given prisms throughout; there is no assertion that separately chosen homotopy inverses commute strictly. Only that $p$ is simplicial is used, not an inner-fibration hypothesis.

title: Fixed-edge triangle prism gives coherent precomposition
statement:
Use quasicategories, fixed-endpoint arrow spaces and left-pinch maps as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [lem-coef-infinity-left-pinch-comparison], and the triangle mapping space and composition classes of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Work in a fixed containing universe. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a simplicial functor of quasicategories, let $s:x\to y$ be an edge of $\mathcal E$, and let $z$ be a vertex. Define $T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)$ degreewise as the simplicial set of $(m+2)$-simplices whose first edge is $s$ and whose face on vertices $2,\ldots,m+2$ is constantly $z$, with operators induced by order maps on those last vertices fixing $0,1$; define $T_{\mathcal B}(p(s),p(z))$ similarly. Let $r_0:T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)\to L_{\mathcal E}(x,z)$ restrict to the face omitting vertex $1$, and let $r_1:T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)\to L_{\mathcal E}(y,z)$ restrict to the face omitting vertex $0$; use the same notation over $\mathcal B$. For every $m$-simplex $t:\Delta^{m+2}\to\mathcal E$ of $T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)$, precomposition with the map $\Delta^2\times\Delta^m\to\Delta^{m+2}$ induced by the monotone map $[2]\times[m]\to[m+2]$, $(0,i)\mapsto0$, $(1,i)\mapsto1$, $(2,i)\mapsto i+2$, gives an $m$-simplex $e(t)$ of the triangle space $V(x,y,z)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]; this defines a simplicial map $e:T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)\to V(x,y,z)$. Its edge restrictions are $\theta\circ e=(j^Lr_1,c_s)$ and $\ell\circ e=j^Lr_0$, where $\theta,\ell$ are the restrictions of that node, $j^L$ the left-pinch maps of [lem-coef-infinity-left-pinch-comparison], and $c_s$ the constant map at the vertex $s$ of $U_{\mathcal E}(x,y)$. Consequently, in homotopy classes of maps $T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)\to U_{\mathcal E}(x,z)$,
$$[j^Lr_0]=[\ell]\,[\theta]^{-1}\bigl([j^Lr_1],[c_s]\bigr),$$
that is, the roof
$$U_{\mathcal E}(y,z)\xleftarrow{\ j^Lr_1\ }T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)\xrightarrow{\ j^Lr_0\ }U_{\mathcal E}(x,z)$$
represents precomposition by $s$ transported to the arrow spaces, and $e$ supplies its triangle witness. The same construction over $\mathcal B$ for $p(s)$ and $p(z)$ gives $e_{\mathcal B}$, and $p\circ e=e_{\mathcal B}\circ p$, $p\circ r_k=r_k\circ p$ $(k=0,1)$ and $p\circ j^L=j^L\circ p$ hold as equalities of simplicial maps; hence the two roofs, their triangle witnesses and the vertical maps induced by $p$ form a strictly commuting diagram, which presents the precomposition square for $s$ and $p(s)$ together with its commutation data.
